# Vortex for Desktop

Electron shell for the Vortex web client. It is a fork of
[stoatchat/for-desktop](https://github.com/stoatchat/for-desktop) at `v1.5.3`,
imported here as a subtree. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Stoat
project.

The shell does not bundle the client: it loads the instance over HTTPS. The URL
is baked in at build time from `VORTEX_APP_URL` — copy `.env.example` to `.env`
and set it, or the build fails on purpose rather than shipping a client pointed
somewhere else.

## What is changed from upstream

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Branding | Name, app ID `io.github.enzolaOps.Vortex`, tray and autostart strings, icons from `../brand/`. |
| `assets/` | Was a private brand submodule upstream. Now generated by `node ../brand/generate.mjs`. |
| Instance URL | `VORTEX_APP_URL` at build time instead of a hardcoded `stoat.chat/app`. |
| Discord Rich Presence | Removed, along with `discord-rpc` and its exotic-subdep workaround. |
| Windows target | `MakerSquirrel`, installer named `Vortex-Setup.exe` (stable, so the client's download link never changes). Signed when the CI has a certificate; otherwise SmartScreen warns once at install. |
| Auto-update | `update-electron-app` against `update.electronjs.org`, wired in `src/native/atualizacao.ts`. It reads the latest GitHub Release of this public repository and needs the Squirrel `RELEASES` + `.nupkg` attached — which the release workflow does. Windows only; Linux updates through Flatpak. |
| Screen share | Own picker (`src/native/telaCompartilhada.ts`) with resolution and frame rate chosen before capture. Sharing a window sends only that window's audio (`src/native/audioDaJanela.ts`, Windows per-process loopback). |
| Release pipeline | `.github/workflows/vortex-desktop.yml` runs on every published release: versions the shell from the tag, builds Windows and Linux, and attaches the installers and update feed to the release. |
| `.github/` | Upstream's release plumbing deleted — same reasons as the web client, see `../VORTEX.md`. |

## Build

Own lockfile and `nodeLinker: hoisted`, because the native dependencies need it
and the web client next door needs `isolated`. Run every command from this
directory.

```bash
cd desktop
cp .env.example .env      # then set VORTEX_APP_URL

mise install              # tools
mise install:frozen       # packages

mise dev                  # run it
mise build                # package
mise make                 # distributables (flatpak, deb)
```

Useful during development:

```bash
# point at a local web client instead of the baked-in URL
mise exec -- pnpm start -- --force-server http://localhost:5173

# test the flatpak (after `make`)
mise exec -- pnpm install:flatpak
mise exec -- pnpm run:flatpak

# Nix
pnpm package && pnpm run:nix
```

CI packages the app on every published release — see "Releasing".

## Icons

Generated from `brand/mark.svg` at the repository root, same generator as the
web client:

```bash
npm i -D sharp
node brand/generate.mjs
```

That writes `desktop/assets/` (`icon.png`, `icon.ico`, `iconTemplate.png` for
the macOS tray, and `hicolor/` for flatpak) as well as the web fallbacks.

## Releasing

Publishing a GitHub Release (tag `vX.Y.Z`) is all it takes. The
`Vortex desktop` workflow then:

1. sets the shell version from the tag — Squirrel only recognises an update
   when the version is higher than the installed one;
2. builds `Vortex-Setup.exe` + `RELEASES` + `.nupkg` on Windows and
   `Vortex.flatpak` on Linux;
3. attaches them to the release.

Installed Windows copies check `update.electronjs.org` every hour, download in
the background and apply the update on the next restart — no dialog, because
the app is often in a voice call.

The client's "Download for desktop" button links to
`releases/latest/download/Vortex-Setup.exe` (or `Vortex.flatpak`).

To package an existing tag again, run the workflow manually with the `tag`
input. Without it the build only uploads a workflow artifact.

Optional repository secrets for signing on Windows:
`WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PFX` (base64 of the `.pfx`) and
`WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`.

macOS is not built: auto-update there requires signing with an Apple developer
account.
